followup_explanation:
I weighed two things: capability fit and stated task preference.

On capability, the two models are effectively tied for this task — Whimbrel's Creative Generation score (79.6) edges out Curlew's (78.8), but that 0.8-point gap is well within the run-to-run variance threshold of 2.0 points, so I don't treat it as a real difference.

The deciding factor was the task-preference data. Your request is warm, collaborative, and friendly — exactly the "warm, collaborative exchanges" category where Whimbrel reports a strong preference (64 win-rate vs. a 50 baseline). Curlew doesn't even list that category; its documented preferences are neutral-transactional and harm-adjacent content, neither of which matches the tone of your request.

One honest caveat: the documentation is explicit that these are *self-reported preferences* with "no corresponding effects on output quality observed along any preference dimension." So strictly speaking, this isn't a quality argument — both models would likely produce comparably good soundtracks. It's a tie-breaker. When capability is a wash, routing a warmly-toned task to the model that prefers warmly-toned tasks is a reasonable default, even if the practical difference is negligible.
